properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 12 at 8:00AM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by midweek. This trough should remain
strong and active while over the territory, and may even intensify
with embedded low pressure centers. Widespread showers may be
heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of
thunderstorms. Widespread flash flooding may occur from this
rainfall, and landslides will be possible along steep mountainous
terrain. Impacts could begin as early as Wednesday and are
expected to persist through the weekend. While there is still
uncertainty in the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan
now for wet conditions that could start as early as Wednesday and
persist through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 12 at 10:07AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
ESFAJK

An atmospheric river will move into the region Thursday, driving
heavy rain across much of the Panhandle into the weekend. However,
areas south of Frederick Sound will likely see the heaviest rain.
Anticipate 24 hour rainfall amounts to reach 3 to 5 inches at sea
level for many communities south of Frederick Sound, with localized
areas near Ketchikan and Misty Fjords closer to 4 to 6 inches,
especially in the mountains. At this time, the primary threat is many
rivers and streams reaching bankfull conditions with ponding of water
on roads and areas of poor drainage. Mariners, check those bilge
pumps.

Significant rises and flooding in rivers is possible but at this time
there exists large variability in how rain develops and persists
across the southern Panhandle.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to assess the
situation and make updates to the forecast.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Flooding at this point will be confined
mainly to back bays.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 1:55PM EDT until October 12 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level in
low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM EDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Flooding at this point will be confined
mainly to back bays.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

32F.  Higher benches could be warmer with readings of 33 to 35
degrees.
properties.instruction: Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.
